proof.text: First check that the mapping-space criteria apply. The standard simplex $\Delta^n$ is a quasicategory directly from its monotone-map description: an inner horn $\Lambda_i^m\to\Delta^n$ specifies vertices $v_0,\ldots,v_m$. Every consecutive edge lies in the horn, so $v_0\leq\cdots\leq v_m$. This sequence defines a simplex of $\Delta^n$, and its restrictions agree with the given horn, since a simplex of $\Delta^n$ is determined by its ordered vertices. By the relative marked-anodyne calculus, a cartesian fibration over a quasicategory has quasicategorical total space. Thus $Y$ and $\Delta^n$ are quasicategories, and $p$ is an inner fibration by the definition of cartesian fibration. Put $u=p(z)$, $v=p(a)$ and $w=p(b)$. The hypotheses and the image of the edge $e$ give $u\leq v\leq w$.

source.place: Standard simplex definition, Section 1.1.2; cartesian fibrations over quasicategories, Section 2.4.2 and Remark 3.1.1.10. The inner-horn verification is written out here.

proof.text: Compute the two base mapping spaces in the right-pinched convention. For vertices $i\leq j$ of $\Delta^n$, an $m$-simplex of $\operatorname{Map}_{\Delta^n}(i,j)$ is a monotone map $[m+1]\to[n]$ taking $0,\ldots,m$ to $i$ and $m+1$ to $j$. There is exactly one such map in every degree, and all operators preserve it. Therefore this mapping simplicial set is canonically $\Delta^0$. Applying this to $(u,v)$ and $(u,w)$, both spaces $\operatorname{Map}_{\Delta^n}(u,v)$ and $\operatorname{Map}_{\Delta^n}(u,w)$ are points. Postcomposition with $p(e)$ is the unique map between them.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.4.3 specialized to a standard simplex; explicit calculation from the right-pinched mapping-space definition.

proof.text: Apply the Cartesian mapping-space criterion to the inner fibration $p:Y\to\Delta^n$, its Cartesian edge $e:a\to b$, and the vertex $z$. It gives a homotopy pullback square with upper row $e\circ-:\operatorname{Map}_Y(z,a)\to\operatorname{Map}_Y(z,b)$ and lower row $\operatorname{Map}_{\Delta^n}(u,v)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\Delta^n}(u,w)$. By step 2 the lower row is the identity of the point. Write $B=\operatorname{Map}_Y(z,b)$. The path-space homotopy fiber product in the criterion is consequently $B\times_{\Delta^0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\Delta^0)\times_{\Delta^0}\Delta^0$, canonically $B$: all coordinates except the $B$ coordinate are unique. Under this identification the comparison from the upper left corner is exactly $e\circ-$. Its weak homotopy equivalence is precisely the assertion that this square is a homotopy pullback. Hence postcomposition by $e$ is a weak homotopy equivalence on the right-pinched mapping spaces.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.4.3, printed p. 131, Cartesian mapping-square criterion; the reduction of its path-space pullback over points is written out.

proof.text: Apply the postcomposition clause of the rigidification comparison with $S=Y$, $h=e$, and its source vertex $w=z$ (the letter $w$ in that comparison is independent of the base vertex named in step 1). Its hypotheses hold by step 1, and step 3 supplies the required weak equivalence on quasicategorical mapping spaces. Its conclusion is that the actual simplicial composition map $[e]\circ-:\mathfrak C[Y](z,a)\to\mathfrak C[Y](z,b)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. This is the specified map in the statement, including its particular edge vertex; the cited comparison requires no Kan condition on the coherent realization mapping sets.

title: Coherent mapping-space comparison along a Cartesian edge over a simplex
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, standard simplices and weak homotopy equivalences as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], cartesian fibrations and cartesian edges as in [lem-coef-relative-marked-anodyne-calculus], and coherent realization $\mathfrak C$, mapping simplicial sets and enriched composition as in [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. Let $n\geq1$ and let $p:Y\to\Delta^n$ be a small cartesian fibration. Let $e:a\to b$ be a $p$-cartesian edge and let $z$ be a vertex of $Y$ with $p(z)\leq p(a)$. The vertex $[e]\in\mathfrak C[Y](a,b)_0$ induces a weak homotopy equivalence of simplicial sets
$$\mathfrak C[Y](z,a)\xrightarrow{[e]\circ-}\mathfrak C[Y](z,b).$$
